apex.config.apex-far-terrain.distance.de: Only used when Unlimited Distance is off: how far (in chunks) Apex Far Terrain draws. This is Apex's own setting and does not depend on Minecraft's render distance: Apex draws wherever the game itself is not drawing terrain, up to this distance.

apex.config.apex-far-terrain.enabled.des: Apex's own lightweight far terrain, on by default: draws chunks you have already seen wherever the game is not drawing them, with real block textures, biome colours, daylight and block light. Every block you could see from outside is kept, including what is under bridges, overhangs and open roofs; sealed caves and hidden blocks are not. Each island is recorded separately; your own Private Island and Garden are kept per profile. Works with or without other rendering mods, on any GPU. How far it draws is set by its own Distance settings, not by Minecraft's render distance. Turns itself off when another far-terrain (LOD) mod is installed.

apex.config.apex-far-terrain.unlimited-d: On (default): draw every recorded chunk, however far away. Off: stop at the Distance setting. Apex can only draw chunks you have been near, so the visible range grows as you explore. Independent of Minecraft's render distance.

apex.config.connected-textures.connected: Framed full blocks join into one surface with neighbours of the same block: copper (waxed or not), iron, gold, diamond, lapis and netherite blocks, quartz block, smooth stone, polished stones (andesite, diorite, granite, deepslate, blackstone, tuff, cinnabar, sulfur), cut sandstone (rows), purpur pillars (same direction) and bookshelves (rows). The frames are made from your current textures, so resource packs keep working. Joined blocks show one continuous surface: the outline and bevel lines between them go away and only the outer edge of the group keeps its border. Works in normal terrain; Apex Far Terrain draws these blocks plain unless "Connected textures in far terrain" is on. On by default; separate from Connected textures (glass).

Off: Apex Far Terrain draws glass and connected blocks plain, each block with its own frame. On: far terrain joins them too, the same way as normal terrain (only for the families switched on above), using the blocks it recorded. Changing it rebuilds far terrain once, a few regions at a time. Off by default.

Glass, stained glass, tinted glass and glass panes join into one smooth surface with neighbouring blocks of the same kind: the frame lines between them go away and only the outer edge stays. Stained glass only joins the same colour. Panes stacked on top of each other also lose the stripe between them. Works in normal terrain (with or without other renderers and shaders); Apex Far Terrain draws glass plain unless "Connected textures in far terrain" is on. On by default.
